claims.claim: Shayne Coplan announced Polymarket launched an AI compute marketplace pricing on-demand rental rates for Nvidia H100, B200 and B300 GPUs with terms to December 2028.
claims.episode_span: the platform has launched an AI compute marketplace that prices on-demand rental rates for Nvidia’s H100, B200 and B300, with terms out to December 2028
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals
claims.supporting_quote: Polymarket founder and CEO Shayne Coplan publicly announced that the platform has launched an AI compute marketplace, enabling open pricing for on-demand rental rates of NVIDIA’s three leading GPUs—H100, B200, and B300—with contract terms extending as far as two years ahead, to December 2028.

claims.claim: Polymarket’s compute contracts are cash-settled binaries on whether a monthly average rental rate exceeds a threshold, with an example of the H100 average in December 2026 exceeding $3 per GPU-hour.
claims.episode_span: the write-up’s example is an H100 average above $3 per GPU-hour in December 2026
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals
claims.supporting_quote: For example, “Will the average rental rate for H100 in December 2026 exceed $3/GPU·hour?”

claims.claim: The settlement benchmark described for Polymarket’s compute contracts is the OCPI index, compiled from actual on-demand rental transactions rather than list prices and available on the Bloomberg Terminal.
claims.episode_span: settled to the OCPI index of actual on-demand rentals rather than cloud list prices, available on the Bloomberg Terminal
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals
claims.supporting_quote: The settlement benchmark is the OCPI index, which is compiled from actual on-demand rental transactions rather than cloud provider list prices and is available on the Bloomberg Terminal.

claims.claim: Coplan said the entire AI economy is built on these prices and that until now there had been no public market to reveal their future trajectory.
claims.episode_span: The entire AI economy is built on these prices, yet until now, there has been no public market to reveal their future trajectory.
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals
claims.supporting_quote: “The entire AI economy is built on these prices, yet until now, there has been no public market to reveal their future trajectory.”

claims.claim: Kalshi launched GPU rental price prediction contracts as early as March 2026 covering H100, H200, B200, A100 and RTX 5090, settled against the Ornn index, and in July released market-implied forward curves.
claims.episode_span: Kalshi has listed GPU rental contracts since March 2026, covering the H100, H200, B200, A100 and RTX 5090 against the Ornn index, and in July published market-implied forward curves
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals
claims.supporting_quote: Kalshi launched GPU rental price prediction contracts as early as March 2026, covering H100, H200, B200, A100, RTX 5090, and others, settled against the Ornn index, and in July released market-implied forward curves based on these contracts.

claims.claim: The Ornn Index showed approximately $3.21 per GPU-hour for H100, $6.48 for H200, $9.74 for B200 and $10.88 for B300.
claims.episode_span: The Ornn index showed about $3.21 per GPU-hour for the H100, $6.48 for the H200, $9.74 for the B200 and $10.88 for the B300
claims.source_title: PolyMarket launches AI compute market, introduces forward pricing for GPU rentals

claims.claim: Polymarket’s early implied curve put H100 rental rates around $2.14 by the end of 2028, a decline of over 30 percent, on thin volume.
claims.episode_span: Polymarket’s early implied curve put the H100 near $2.14 by the end of 2028, a decline of more than 30 percent, on volume still in the tens of thousands of dollars

claims.supporting_quote: Polymarket's early implied price curve shows that the market generally expects a long-term decline in GPU rental rates, with H100 prices potentially falling to around $2.14 by the end of 2028, a decline of over 30%.

claims.claim: A paper finds a stable no-trade Nash equilibrium only when almost rational agents have slightly different computational power, and that identical power may fail to converge.
claims.episode_span: a stable no-trade outcome, a Nash equilibrium, is reached only when “almost rational” agents have slightly different computational power
claims.source_title: Will AI Trade? A Computational Inversion of the No-Trade Theorem
claims.supporting_quote: Our central finding inverts the classic paradigm: a stable no-trade outcome (Nash equilibrium) is reached only when "almost rational" agents have slightly different computational power.

claims.claim: A paper argues that private information which verifies a security’s true value offers insights for insider trading, illiquidity, and trading that uses public blockchains and oracles.
claims.episode_span: insider trading, the link between no-trade results and markets that look illiquid, and trading that uses public blockchains and oracles
claims.source_title: No Trade Under Verifiable Information
claims.supporting_quote: We argue that these conditions can offer insights in three different settings: insider trading, the connection of low liquidity in markets with no trade, and trading using public blockchains and oracles.
